questions.problem: Use the first three terms of the binomial expansion of $(1+x)^{7}$ in ascending powers of $x$ to approximate $(1.12)^{7}.$ Give your answer to four decimal places.
questions.worked_solution:
Recall that when $n$ is a positive integer, 

$$
(1+x)^{n}=1+nx+\frac{1}{2!}n(n-1){x}^{2}+⋯+{x}^{n}.
$$

Therefore, 

$$
\begin{aligned}{(1+x)}^{7} & =1+7x+\frac{1}{2}\cdot 7\cdot 6\cdot {x}^{2}+⋯+{x}^{7} \\  & =1+7x+21{x}^{2}+⋯+{x}^{7}.\end{aligned}
$$

So, for small $x,$ we have

$$
{(1+x)}^{7}≈1+7x+21{x}^{2}.
$$

Finally, we substitute $x=0.12$ into the above approximation of $(1+x)^{7}:$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}(1.12)^{7} & =(1+0.12)^{7} \\  & ≈1+7(0.12)+21(0.12)^{2} \\  & =1+7(0.12)+21(0.014\,4) \\  & =1+0.84+0.302\,4 \\  & =2.142\,4,\end{aligned}
$$

to four decimal places.

questions.problem: Calculate the percentage error obtained when approximating the value of $(1.02)^{7}$ using the first three terms of the binomial expansion of $(1+x)^{7}$ in ascending powers of $x.$ Round your final percentage error to two decimal places.
questions.worked_solution:
Recall that when $n$ is a positive integer, 

$$
(1+x)^{n}=1+nx+\frac{1}{2!}n(n-1){x}^{2}+⋯+{x}^{n}.
$$

Therefore, 

$$
\begin{aligned}{(1+x)}^{7} & =1+7x+\frac{1}{2!}\cdot 7\cdot 6\cdot {x}^{2}+⋯+{x}^{n} \\  & =1+7x+21{x}^{2}+⋯+{x}^{n}.\end{aligned}
$$

So, for small $x,$ we have

$$
{(1+x)}^{7}≈1+7x+21{x}^{2}.
$$

Now, we substitute $x=0.02$ into the above approximation of $(1+x)^{7}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}(1.02)^{7} & =(1+0.02)^{7} \\  & ≈1+7(0.02)+21(0.02)^{2} \\  & =1+7(0.02)+21(0.000\,4) \\  & =1+0.14+0.008\,4 \\  & =1.148\,4\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, using a calculator, we can compute the percentage error, as follows: 

$$
\begin{aligned}%\,error & =\frac{\text{amount of error}}{\text{exact value}}\times 100 \\  & =\frac{|(1.02)^{7}-1.148\,4|}{(1.02)^{7}}\times 100 \\  & ≈0.02%\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to two decimal places.

questions.problem: Calculate the percentage error obtained when approximating the value of $(1.98)^{5}$ using the first three terms of the binomial expansion of $(2+x)^{5}$ in ascending powers of $x.$ Round your final percentage error to one decimal place.
questions.worked_solution:
The binomial theorem for positive integer $n$ states that

$$
(a+b)^{n}=(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{n}{0}){a}^{n}{b}^{0}+(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{n}{1}){a}^{n-1}{b}^{1}+(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{n}{2}){a}^{n-2}{b}^{2}+…+(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{n}{n}){a}^{0}{b}^{n}.
$$

By substituting $a=2,$ $b=x,$ and $n=5,$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{(2+x)}^{5} & =(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{5}{0}){(2)}^{5}{(x)}^{0}+(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{5}{1}){(2)}^{5-1}{(x)}^{1}+(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{5}{2}){(2)}^{5-2}{(x)}^{2}+⋯ \\  & =1{(2)}^{5}+5{(2)}^{4}{(x)}^{1}+10{(2)}^{3}{(x)}^{2}+⋯ \\  & =1(32)+5(16)(x)+10(8)({x}^{2})+⋯ \\  & =32+80x+80{x}^{2}+⋯\,.\end{aligned}
$$

So, for small $x,$ we have

$$
{(2+x)}^{5}≈32+80x+80{x}^{2}.
$$

Now, we substitute $x=-0.02$ into the above approximation of $(2+x)^{5}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}(1.98)^{5} & =(2+(-0.02))^{5} \\  & ≈32+80(-0.02)+80(-0.02)^{2} \\  & =32-80(0.02)+80(0.000\,4) \\  & =32-1.6+0.032 \\  & =30.432\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, using a calculator, we can compute the percentage error, as follows: 

$$
\begin{aligned}%\,error & =\frac{\text{amount of error}}{\text{exact value}}\times 100 \\  & =\frac{|(1.98)^{5}-30.432|}{(1.98)^{5}}\times 100 \\  & ≈0.0%\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to one decimal place.

$$
(a+b)^{n}=(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{n}{0}){a}^{n}{b}^{0}+(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{n}{1}){a}^{n-1}{b}^{1}+(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{n}{2}){a}^{n-2}{b}^{2}+…+(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{n}{n}){a}^{0}{b}^{n}.
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}{(3+x)}^{5} & =(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{5}{0}){(3)}^{5}{(x)}^{0}+(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{5}{1}){(3)}^{5-1}{(x)}^{1}+(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{5}{2}){(3)}^{5-2}{(x)}^{2}+⋯ \\  & =1{(3)}^{5}+5{(3)}^{4}{(x)}^{1}+10{(3)}^{3}{(x)}^{2}+⋯ \\  & =243+5(81)(x)+10(27)({x}^{2})+⋯ \\  & =243+405x+270{x}^{2}+⋯\,.\end{aligned}
$$

So, for small $x,$ we have

$$
{(3+x)}^{5}≈243+405x+270{x}^{2}
$$

Now, we substitute $x=0.2$ into the above approximation of $(3+x)^{5}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}(3.2)^{5} & =(3+0.2)^{5} \\  & ≈243+405(0.2)+270(0.2)^{2} \\  & =243+405(0.2)+270(0.0\,4) \\  & =243+81+10.8 \\  & =334.8\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, using a calculator, we can compute the percentage error, as follows: 

$$
\begin{aligned}%\,error & =\frac{\text{amount of error}}{\text{exact value}}\times 100 \\  & =\frac{|(3.2)^{5}-334.8|}{(3.2)^{5}}\times 100 \\  & ≈0.2%\end{aligned}

rounded to one decimal place.

$$
(a+b)^{n}=(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{n}{0}){a}^{n}{b}^{0}+(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{n}{1}){a}^{n-1}{b}^{1}+(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{n}{2}){a}^{n-2}{b}^{2}+…+(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{n}{n}){a}^{0}{b}^{n}.
$$

By substituting $a=2,$ $b=x,$ and $n=5,$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{(2+x)}^{5} & =(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{5}{0}){(2)}^{5}{(x)}^{0}+(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{5}{1}){(2)}^{5-1}{(x)}^{1}+(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{5}{2}){(2)}^{5-2}{(x)}^{2}+⋯ \\  & =1{(2)}^{5}+5{(2)}^{4}{(x)}^{1}+10{(2)}^{3}{(x)}^{2}+⋯ \\  & =1(32)+5(16)(x)+10(8)({x}^{2})+⋯ \\  & =32+80x+80{x}^{2}+⋯\,.\end{aligned}
$$

$$
{(2+x)}^{5}≈32+80x+80{x}^{2}.

$$

canonical_examples.problem: Use the first four terms of the binomial expansion of $(1+x)^6$ in ascending powers of $x$ to approximate $(1.15)^6.$ Give your answer to three decimal places.
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
Recall that when $n$ is a positive integer, 

$$
(1+x)^n = 1 + nx + \dfrac{1}{2!} n(n-1)x^2 + \dfrac{1}{3!} n(n-1)(n-2)x^3 + \cdots + x^n.
$$

Therefore, 

$$
\begin{aligned}{(1+x)}^{6} & =1+6x+\frac{1}{2}\cdot 6\cdot 5\cdot {x}^{2}+\frac{1}{6}\cdot 6\cdot 5\cdot 4\cdot {x}^{3}+⋯+{x}^{n} \\  & =1+6x+15{x}^{2}+20{x}^{3}+⋯\,+{x}^{n}.\end{aligned}
$$

So, for small $x,$ we have

$$
\left( {1 + x} \right)^6 \approx 1 + 6x + 15x^2 + 20x^3.
$$

Finally, we substitute $x=0.15$ into the above approximation of $(1 + x)^6{:}$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}(1.15)^{6} & =(1+0.15)^{6} \\  & ≈1+6(0.15)^{1}+15(0.15)^{2}+20(0.15)^{3} \\  & =1+6(0.15)+15(0.022\,5)+20(0.003\,375) \\  & =1+0.9+0.337\,5+0.067\,5 \\  & =2.305,\end{aligned}
$$

to three decimal places.

canonical_examples.problem: Calculate the percentage error obtained when approximating the value of $(1.08)^{5}$ using the first three terms of the binomial expansion of $(1+x)^5$ in ascending powers of $x.$ Round your final percentage error to two decimal places.
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
The binomial theorem for positive integer $n$ states that

$$
{(a + b)^n} = {n \choose 0}{a^n}{b^0} + {n \choose 1}{a^{n - 1}}{b^1} + {n \choose 2}{a^{n - 2}}{b^2} +  \ldots  + {n \choose n}{a^0}{b^n}.
$$

By substituting $a = 1,$ $b = x,$ and $n = 5,$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{(1+x)}^{5} & =(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{5}{0}){(1)}^{5}{(x)}^{0}+(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{5}{1}){(1)}^{5-1}{(x)}^{1}+(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{5}{2}){(1)}^{5-2}{(x)}^{2}+⋯ \\  & =1{(1)}^{5}+5{(1)}^{4}{(x)}^{1}+10{(1)}^{3}{(x)}^{2}+⋯ \\  & =1+5(1)(x)+10(1)({x}^{2})+⋯ \\  & =1+5x+10{x}^{2}+⋯\,.\end{aligned}
$$

So, for small $x,$ we have

$$
{\left( {1 + x} \right)^{5}} \approx 1 + 5x + 10x^2.
$$

Now, we substitute $x = 0.08$ into the above approximation of $(1 + x)^5{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}(1.08)^{5} & =(1+0.08)^{5} \\  & ≈1+5(0.08)+10(0.08)^{2} \\  & =1+5(0.08)+10(0.006\,4) \\  & =1+0.4+0.064 \\  & =1.464\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, using a calculator, we can compute the percentage error, as follows: 

$$
\begin{aligned}%\,error & =\frac{\text{amount of error}}{\text{exact value}}\times 100 \\  & =\frac{|(1.08)^{5}-1.464|}{(1.08)^{5}}\times 100 \\  & ≈0.36%\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to two decimal places.
